Hi John / Priya,

Thanks for the call this morning - good alignment on the high-level SLOs. Quick recap and next steps so we can move the network qualification to your infra team:

Recap (from our discussion):
- Performance targets: p95 generation latency <= 150ms (single-request streaming case), p99 <= 300ms for non-streaming.
- Throughput/concurrency: expected steady-state ~120 requests/sec, peak bursts up to 400 rps. Concurrent model sessions ~150.
- Streaming: we need stable bi-directional streaming with server-side token flushes <= 50ms when available.
- Payloads: typical prompt size ~1.5k tokens, response length ~200 tokens.

Network qualification items (what we need from Acme):
1) VPC topology diagram (attached: acme_vpc_topology.pdf) and public-facing/peering subnets.
2) Preferred connectivity: VPN vs Cloud Peering. If peering is possible, we recommend it for latency-sensitive workloads.
3) Outbound egress requirements: list of IP ranges and ports we will provide (see action items).
4) Traceroutes/iperf tests from a representative app host to our peering endpoints (we'll provide targets).

Action owners / next steps:
- Marissa (me): schedule a 45-min network deep-dive with your infra and SRE teams next week; share Redwood's egress IP ranges and port list.
- Jordan: share our VPN/peering checklist and sample routing config.
- John / Priya: share VPC topology and confirm whether cross-account peering is an option, and who on your infra team will own the tests.

Attachments: acme_vpc_topology.pdf

If you confirm availability, I can send a calendar invite for Wed or Thu next week. Thanks - we want to make sure the network path keeps the end-to-end RTT low enough to meet the SLOs.

Hi John - great questions, answers below.

1) Latency split (approximate expectations):
- Network RTT budget (app host <-> Redwood edge / peering point): target <= 30ms (one-way ~15ms). This keeps the network portion comfortably below 40-50ms p95.
- Model inference + tokenization + queuing: target p95 ~80-100ms depending on model and sequence length.
- Application processing: the remaining ~10-30ms.

So with a network RTT <= 30ms and our optimized serving runtime you should be able to hit p95 <= 150ms in most steady-state cases for the prompt/response sizes we discussed. If your RTT is higher, we can recommend warm-routing to closer Redwood edge points or consider model sharding.

2) VPN vs Peering:
- Peering (recommended): lowest latency and most predictable jitter. Requires a peering arrangement in your cloud account; we'll provide peering prefixes and routes to accept.
- VPN (supported): works fine but tends to add ~10-40ms of additional latency and potential jitter depending on VPN appliance. Yes - we provide stable egress IP ranges for NAT through Redwood-managed gateways when using VPN.

3) Test endpoints and ports (summary):
- TCP ports: 443 (TLS), 5222 (optional health probe), 80 (health redirect).
- Recommended iperf config: 30s TCP test, parallel streams = 8, MTU 1500. Please run tests at peak/steady hours and off-peak to characterize variance.
- Traceroute: ICMP + TCP to port 443.

We'll attach the detailed checklist (vpn-checklist.xlsx) and our current egress CIDR block list in the deep-dive materials.

Next steps:
- Jordan: can you attach the checklist and push calendar invite for Thu 31 Mar 2028 09:30 PT (tentative)?
- John / Priya: confirm the infra owner who will run traceroutes and iperf and share access to VPC topology diagram.

Thanks - looping Aditya for any model-level notes on concurrency behavior (Aditya: can you confirm whether session-level KV cache warmup will add any startup latency we should call out?).

Best,
Marissa
